_comment: AWS's P-EAGLE drafters (arXiv 2602.01469): EAGLE-3 trained to draft every token of a step in one forward, its rows past the newest reading learned placeholders (the `ptd_token_id` token's embedding and `mask_hidden`, which vLLM's `parallel_drafting` loads the same way). It ships as its own checkpoint with its own config, whose `architectures` reads `LlamaForCausalLM`, so it names its target config (`head_targets`). It drafts only when `--speculative-model` names a checkpoint of it (`spec/mtp` compiles it): AWS publishes only its bf16 drafter, which reads 1.4 GB a pass, and no conversion of it is published yet. Two drafts a step (`spec_drafts`), measured on a base M5 (gpt-oss-20b at MLX 4-bit, one request, greedy) over the model card's benchmarks, 10 prompts each of MT-Bench, HumanEval and GSM-8K to 1024 tokens: two drafts accept 2.38 / 2.34 / 2.59 tokens a step (the card's three, on an H200, 2.75 / 2.96 / 2.83 to these 2.79 / 2.71 / 3.15) and run 66.1 / 63.8 / 70.5 tok/s against 57.3 / 57.2 / 56.8 alone; one 63.8 / 61.7 / 65.2, three 64.9 / 60.8 / 70.6, four 65.5 / 62.3 / 72.2. A verify step's MoE reads each row's experts, so its rows cost far more than a dense target's: 2 / 4 / 8 rows cost 1.40 / 2.06 / 3.18x a decode step. Its KV pass over a prompt runs after the step that gives the first token, so time to first token is its target's on a prompt of one chunk (301 / 302 ms at 560 tokens, 951-966 / 957-979 at 1920) and pays only the chunks before the last on a longer one (+12% at 5864). Its tensors sit at the file's top level (`decoder_safetensors_prefix` empty): its first layer as `midlayer.*`, the rest as `layers.<L>.*`. The `-mixed` stem is an MLX conversion at group 64 — MLPs at 3 bits, attention and `fc` at 4, the embedding at 8 — that drafts as many tokens a step as one with attention and the embedding at 8 bits: a 4-bit embedding loses most of the mask rows' acceptance (an MLX transcription of vLLM's drafter: 2.30 -> 1.80 tokens a step). It borrows only its target's lm_head (`borrows`): AWS froze it in training, so the drafter's own copy is the target's bit for bit; its embedding it trained, so that one is its own. It drafts over its target vocabulary's first 65536 ids (`vocab_size`, the lm_head rows it reads), as Qwen3.5's head does; its embedding keeps every id (`embed_vocab_size`), the mask token's (201020) among them. `target_hidden_size` is the width of the three target hidden states `fc` fuses.
